Do you enjoy working with data, economic analysis and solving complex problems? Can you turn numbers and insights into meaningful solutions that contribute to a more sustainable future? Are you looking to apply your academic knowledge to real-life projects while gaining valuable experience in a leading consulting company? Then you might be our new Economist Student Helper!

Create the solutions that will shape a better tomorrow

COWI is experiencing growing activity within sustainability, the environment, energy, demographics, transport and socioeconomic impact assessments. To further strengthen our team, we are looking for a student assistant to join our department. We are a team of fourteen colleagues, within life cycle assessments, sustainability and socio-economic analysis, who work closely with our clients on some of Denmark’s most significant projects across sectors. As a student assistant in the LCA, Sustainability and Socioeconomics department, you will have the opportunity to turn data and economic analysis into solutions to real societal challenges. You will gain insight into how we work with different types of clients, including ministries, government agencies and private companies.

As a student assistant at COWI, you will gain experience across a variety of projects and clients, expand your professional toolkit and build a solid foundation for your future career.

Furthermore, you will be responsible for:

• Conducting data analysis and supporting economic modelling.

• Contributing to proposal writing and the preparation of final client deliverables.

• Assisting in report writing, research and presentation material

• Tackling challenging problems that require creative thinking.

• Being open to learning new software, tools and methods.

• Managing tasks effectively and meeting deadlines.

Your skills. Our team. Together, we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

Furthermore you should have:

• A bachelors or masters degree in Economics, Political Science, Business Administration, Agricultural economics or similar field

• Experience in economic and statistical analysis with an interest in green transition.

• Advanced Excel proficiency and a well-developed quantitative skill set along with knowledge in Python

• The ability to work and collaborate effectively within diverse, multi-disciplinary project teams

• Effective communication skills, both written and verbal in Danish and English, with the ability to present technical findings clearly and professionally to colleagues and clients

• Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office

• Commitment to quality, precision and technical excellence

Working hours and flexibility

You will be employed on an hourly paid contract, with a standard working time of eight hours per week. We offer flexibility during exam periods, and there may also be periods when it would be beneficial if you could work additional hours.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Do you have more questions?

For more information about the position and what we offer, please reach out to Economist Emil Nelander EMNL@COWI.COM.

Learn more about our projects, strategy, ambitions and life at COWI at www.cowi.com.

We are committed to a respectful and equitable workplace where every colleague feels a sense of belonging and has equal opportunities to thrive and develop. We expect our leaders to model inclusive leadership and foster a culture that values different perspectives and ideas. Diversity and inclusion inform our relevant decisions and processes, as well as the way we bring teams and forums together. This reflects our values and our belief that it is the right thing to do.

Do you want to lead ICT management and digital delivery on complex civil infrastructure projects? Can you translate contractual and project-specific ICT requirements into clear governance, practical workflows and successful technical implementation? Are you motivated by bringing clients, project management, engineering disciplines and digital specialists together on projects such as bridges, tunnels, marine structures and other major infrastructure? Then this could be the next step in your career.

Lead ICT management from requirements to implementation

As our new ICT expert, you will lead ICT management, digital governance and digital delivery on multidisciplinary civil infrastructure projects. Our work includes bridges, tunnels, marine structures and other major infrastructure, often involving complex interfaces between disciplines, organisations and project phases.

You will advise clients and project organization, translate contractual and project-specific requirements into practical processes and workflows, and drive their technical implementation in collaboration with project management, engineering disciplines and digital specialists.

The position is a project-based leadership role and combines professional leadership of the ICT process, leadership of the project’s digital delivery and client-facing advice.

Your key responsibilities will include

• Lead ICT management and digital delivery through relevant project phases, from mobilisation and planning to execution and handover.

• Advise clients and project management on ICT requirements, BIM processes, information management and digital governance.

• Prepare, maintain and implement project-specific ICT documentation based on Molio’s ICT paradigms, contractual requirements and relevant industry standards.

• Translate requirements into clear roles, responsibilities, workflows, digital deliverables and quality-assurance procedures.

• Establish the project’s digital delivery framework, including model and information requirements, naming conventions, exchange procedures, coordination processes and Common Data Environment structures.

• Drive the technical implementation of ICT requirements together with project management, engineering disciplines, BIM coordinators, Digital Design specialists and other technical contributors.

• Facilitate ICT kick-off meetings, workshops and coordination activities, ensuring that agreed processes are understood and applied across the project organisation.

• Manage interfaces with internal and external stakeholders, including clients, project managers, discipline leads, architects, contractors, and international delivery teams.

• Identify opportunities for project-specific automation and digital improvements and coordinate their implementation with the relevant specialists.

• Contribute lessons learned and proven workflows to the continued development of COWI’s ICT management practices.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you enjoy creating structure and direction together with others. You communicate clearly, build trusted relationships and can align stakeholders with different technical backgrounds, priorities and contractual responsibilities.

You are motivated by turning requirements and strategies into solutions that work in practice. You understand that successful ICT management requires robust governance as well as active involvement in project implementation.

On top of that, you will have:

• At least 7 years of relevant experience within ICT management, BIM management, digital project delivery or a comparable field in the engineering and construction industry.

• Practical experience leading ICT management or digital delivery on multidisciplinary projects.

• Strong knowledge of Molio’s ICT paradigms and practical experience applying them on multidisciplinary projects.

• Knowledge of relevant Danish industry standards and contractual frameworks, including YBL18 and YBB19 where applicable

• Knowledge of relevant global Industry standards such as ISO 19650

• Experience translating client and contractual requirements into practical digital processes, workflows and deliverables.

• Experience driving technical implementation, for example through Common Data Environment structures, coordination workflows, quality-control procedures, data exchanges or automated checking processes.

• A strong understanding of BIM processes, information management, digital collaboration and multidisciplinary coordination.

• General knowledge of relevant digital delivery applications such as Revit, Tekla, OpenRoadsDesign

• Experience with Coordination and Common Data Environment platforms, such as Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Navisworks; Bentley Infrastructure Cloud and ProjectWise; and Trimble Connect and Quadri—or comparable systems.

• Strong planning, facilitation, communication and stakeholder-management skills.

• Professional proficiency in English and Danish.

You do not need to be a software developer or perform every technical task yourself. However, you must have sufficient technical understanding to define the project’s needs, involve the right specialists, guide implementation and ensure that the resulting solutions are adopted by the project organisation.

Your professional environment

You will become part of Digital Design within Structures and Digital Engineering. We support the delivery of complex civil infrastructure projects, including bridges, tunnels, marine structures and other major infrastructure.

You will work closely with project management, engineering disciplines and digital specialists to establish consistent digital processes across multidisciplinary projects. You will join a collaborative professional environment where knowledge sharing, technical development and practical project value are closely connected.

The role allows you to influence both individual projects and the continued development of our ICT management practices.

We are looking for a leader who combines deep technical insight with people-oriented leadership. You bring the professional credibility to provide direction and challenge when needed, while creating an engaging and collaborative environment where people can perform and grow.

• A degree in Structural Engineering combined with solid experience within structural engineering, consultancy and project-based environments.

Do you have the technical expertise and leadership experience to lead electrical design delivery on large-scale data centre projects?

As Electrical Lead at COWI, you will take a central technical role in some of our largest and most complex data centre projects. You will lead electrical design teams, act as a key technical interface with clients and partners and can shape how COWI develops and delivers electrical design for data centres across the Nordics and internationally. Data centre work experience specifically with hyperscale projects is a requirement for this position. Your work base will be at one of COWI's offices in either Lyngby, Odense, Vejle, Aarhus or Aalborg based on where you live in Denmark.

Grow COWI’s international data centre business

Data centres are a strategic growth area at COWI, and we are continuing to strengthen our capabilities and position in this market. As Electrical Lead, you will combine technical leadership on major projects with significant influence on how we approach electrical design and develop consistent ways of working across our data centre business.

You will work closely with clients, Senior Project Managers, Project Directors, Design Managers and multidisciplinary engineering teams across different project stages. You will work in an English-speaking environment alongside colleagues across the Nordics and the UK.

Your key responsibilities will be to:

• Act as the technical electrical lead towards clients, partners and other external stakeholders, translating project requirements into appropriate technical solutions

• Lead electrical design teams on large-scale data centre projects, with overall responsibility for the electrical design delivery.

• Plan and manage the electrical design process, coordinating resources, activities, interfaces and deliverables across project stages and delivery teams.

• Lead the technical development of data centre electrical power systems and technical architecture, covering critical power, MV/LV distribution, UPS, generators, redundancy and resilience, as well as ICC, BMS and ELV systems and their interfaces with other technical disciplines.

• Ensure technical quality and consistency of the electrical design, providing senior technical direction and supporting key design decisions and complex interfaces.

• Contribute to the continued development of COWI’s data centre capabilities, helping shape our technical approaches and ways of working across projects and international delivery teams.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

To succeed in this role, you combine strong electrical engineering competence with the ability to lead people and complex technical deliveries. You are comfortable taking technical responsibility in demanding project environments and representing the electrical discipline towards clients and project partners.

You have the technical breadth and engineering judgement to lead the overall electrical design delivery and guide specialists across the wider electrical scope. You communicate clearly, work effectively across disciplines and bring a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to complex engineering challenges.

To be considered for this role, you should have:

• A degree in Electrical Engineering or similar.

• Direct experience from large-scale data centre projects.

• Proven experience leading or taking significant technical responsibility for electrical design and engineering in complex projects.

• Strong understanding of data centre electrical design and sufficient technical breadth to lead the wider electrical scope and its key technical interfaces.

• Experience leading engineers or technical teams, combined with the confidence and communication skills to represent the electrical discipline towards clients and senior project stakeholders.

• Strong communication skills in English and the ability to work effectively in international project teams.

• Familiarity with relevant data centre standards and structured delivery frameworks such as EN 50600, TIA-942, RIBA or equivalent is an advantage.

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

Our IoT team builds the devices and edge software that connect our customers' production lines to the Factbird platform, from sensors on the line to industrial edge computers running computer vision right next to the machines. We're a small team with broad ownership, and we're hiring an Embedded Platform Engineer to help build and run the platform our edge products stand on.

**This role is onsite in Copenhagen, Denmark. We welcome applications from candidates based in Germany who are open to relocating to Copenhagen.

**

About the Role

As Embedded Platform Engineer, you'll work hands-on across Factbird EDGE, our industrial edge platform, together with the rest of the IoT team: the operating system, the device software, and the vision models that run on it. You'll take ownership of the infrastructure around the devices: provisioning and recovery, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability, the systems that keep our unattended devices reliable, secure, and safely updatable in factories you may never visit.

You'll work in Rust on embedded Linux, with Yocto, AWS IoT Greengrass, GStreamer and ONNX Runtime at the core, alongside our Cloud and DevOps engineers and the people building our AI capabilities. Part of the job is shaping the role with the team as our edge products grow.

You'll thrive here if you like working across a system end to end, from the bootloader to the cloud connection, and if you'd rather fix the root cause in the build than patch around it on the device.

What you'll do

Embedded Linux & the EDGE platform

• Develop our Yocto-based Linux distribution: layers, BSPs, kernel configuration, and reproducible builds

• Build and maintain the Rust components that run on our edge devices

• Bring up new hardware platforms, debug on target, and keep the platform secure and maintainable over a long device lifetime

• Keep our CI and on-hardware testing healthy, so changes reach devices with confidence

Edge inference & vision

• Work with our ML and vision engineers on the device side of our computer vision capabilities: camera pipelines, video streaming, and model inference that runs efficiently on industrial hardware

• Share ownership with our ML engineers of how trained models move from our model pipeline onto devices and how they perform there: packaging, rollout, rollback, and drift monitoring

• Help bring new edge runtimes for vision workloads from development into production

Fleet infrastructure & ownership

• Own device provisioning, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability

• Make deployments to devices in the field safe and boring: staged rollouts, health checks, and recovery paths

• Help diagnose issues on devices at customer sites, working with Support, Product, and Cloud to turn them into lasting fixes

• Share knowledge in both directions: learn the parts of the platform others built, and make sure what you build doesn't live only in your head

**What we're looking for

**

We're looking for an engineer who has shipped embedded Linux into production and lived with it afterwards: someone who has debugged a device they couldn't touch, and who wants real responsibility rather than a ticket queue.

You work independently, but you don't work alone. You can take a loosely defined problem and move it forward without daily direction, and you pull others in early, because on a small team the best fix is one more than one person understands. You're disciplined where it matters, in releases and rollouts, and curious where it pays off, in vision and new hardware.

You don't need everything below. Yocto is the core. Rust matters, but strong C/C++ engineers who have started with Rust are welcome too. The rest you can grow into with us.

**

The ideal background**

• Hands-on experience shipping embedded Linux to production, including Yocto: layers, BSPs and images you've built and maintained yourself, not just consumed

• Strong systems programming in Rust, or deep C/C++ experience on embedded Linux and real exposure to Rust that you want to build on

• An advantage if you have worked with AWS IoT Core or Greengrass, video pipelines or ML inference on edge hardware, or in industrial settings where devices run unattended for years

• A solid grasp of embedded security and update mechanisms: signed images, A/B or similar update schemes, and secure device provisioning

• You can explain a technical trade-off clearly, whether you're talking to another engineer, Support or a customer, and you do it in fluent English

• We welcome applications from people eager to move to Denmark, as long as you already have the legal right to live and work here.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We'd love to hear from you

**

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at **crva@factbird.com

Do you want to own and drive a critical digital solution that delivers real, measurable impact? Scandlines is looking for a Product Owner (PO) for our Port Automation Solution.

As Product Owner for the Port Automation Solution, you will set direction, drive priorities, and ensure the solution creates tangible value for Scandlines’ customers, operations, and the wider organization.

You will act as the key link between business needs, operational realities, and technical delivery — turning strategy into concrete outcomes. With a strong focus on user value and continuous improvement, you will play a pivotal role in shaping a solution that is both forward-looking and firmly grounded in day-to-day operations.

Scandlines is a modern and innovative ferry operator, running two high-capacity, high-frequency routes with a green ambition for the future. At Scandlines we want to provide the best break on the journey for both passengers and freight customers. The Port Automation Solution has today been rolled out in our Rødby – Puttgarden route, and in short term we wish to rollout the solution in the second route (Gedser – Rostock).  This will be one of the first tasks to look at as the new PO.

As part of the role, you will be functional team leader of the Port Automation Solution team. The team consist of three members situated in both our main office in Havneholmen and in our office in Rostock.

• Facilitate operational governance, including prioritisation, escalation, decision-making, action follow-up, and ongoing monitoring of performance, adoption, risks, and improvements.

• Facilitate requirement clarification sessions and feedback loops, translating user needs into actionable solution requirements.

• Promote a strong user-centric mindset by actively seeking feedback from those who use, operate, or are otherwise impacted by the solution.

• Drive and support change management activities that enable successful adoption of the Port Automation Solution.

• Develop a holistic view of the change impact across processes, roles, behaviours, governance, culture, and ways of working.

• Engage leaders, end users, and key stakeholders to build understanding, ownership, readiness for change, and a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement.

Team Leadership

• Act as team leader for the Port Automation Solution group, providing direction, structure, and prioritisation for the team’s work.

• Support team members in understanding priorities, expectations, dependencies, and decision-making processes.

• Ensure clear objectives, agreed ways of working, and a shared understanding of how success will be measured.

We are looking for a candidate with solid experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, Business Owner, Project Lead, or in a similar role within a digital or process-driven environment. You excel at translating business needs and user insights into clear priorities, actionable requirements, and value-driven roadmaps, and you are comfortable driving stakeholder alignment and decision-making.

We do not expect you to have prior formal leadership experience, but we are looking for someone who is ready and motivated to take on that responsibility. You bring strong people skills, a collaborative mindset, and the confidence to engage, influence, and guide others.

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Animal and Veterinary Sciences programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

The project investigates the potential of maximizing fresh grass forage intake to reduce enteric methane emission and increase nitrogen utilization, while maintaining milk production. A series of trials with lactating dairy cows are planned investigating combinations of grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards.

• A unique opportunity to contribute to a more sustainable agriculture and environmental-friendly milk production

jobs.occupation: Up to 3 PhD fellowships in Quantum error correction
jobs.description:
The Quantum error correction team at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) invites applicants for up to three PhD fellowships.

  The start date is (expected to be) 1 April, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The programme
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Program (NQCP), funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, is building a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge program in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, the ambition is to build a mission-driven full-stack approach which will involve exciting innovations at every level, from the quantum processor to the quantum-classical interface, all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. The vision of the programme is to enable the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve important problems in the life sciences.

  The project
 Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires low logical error rates together with resource-efficient, experimentally feasible approaches to quantum error correction. Our research spans low-overhead quantum error-correcting codes, efficient syndrome extraction, high-fidelity parity measurements, and scalable hardware architectures. We aim to connect these efforts with fault-tolerant logical operations, taking into account the noise characteristics, connectivity, and operational constraints of quantum computing platforms. In our work, we are collaborating closely with all of the different teams at NQCP; see nqcp.ku.dk.

  We are looking for up to three motivated PhD candidates to undertake research within theoretical effort for quantum error-correction. We are interested in developing a project plan with prospective candidates to best match their skills and experience to the activities in the QEC team. We imagine that the candidates would undertake research within one or more of the following topics:

   	
• Investigation of low-overhead and high-threshold error-correctable codes, including low-density parity check codes 	
• Resource estimation and optimization for scalable quantum computing over different hardware platforms 	
• Distributed quantum error correction on modular design and quantum networks 	
• Optimization of syndrome extraction circuits, error correction cycle, and fault-tolerant logical operation   Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of Physics, Computational Physics, Quantum Information, or a closely related field, with a focus on theoretical and/or computational quantum physics.

  Successful candidates will have:

   	
• Strong analytical and computational skills 	
• Strong knowledge of quantum mechanics and quantum information 	
• An interest in developing quantum error correction methods that account for hardware capabilities and limitations 	
• A passion for developing theoretical protocols 	
• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic research environment 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction or quantum computing platforms, including photonic systems and superconducting circuits, is an advantage.   Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by the NNF Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen.

  The project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Maryam Khanahmadi, maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk, QEC team lead, and the principal supervisor will be Stefano Paesani, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk.

  Qualifications needed 
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. a degree in Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Quantum Information or similar. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full-time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Good language and communication skills 	
• Willingness to work in a team 	
• Willingness to engage actively with the other teams at NQCP    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Please note that there is the possibility of including an educational part to the PhD project. Therefore, please indicate in the application whether you would be interested in this.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original degree diplomas and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline
 The deadline for applications is 6 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You will be notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Maryam Khanahmadi: maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a 3-year PhD stipend in the field of quantum control theory for quantum algorithms within the general study programme Electronical and Electronic Engineering, as per January 1st 2027, or soon hereafter.

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Your work tasks

The position is part of the research project QUANTA – Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. Real quantum computers are open quantum systems: noise and decoherence act on the computation while it runs, so the idealised picture of a sequence of perfect unitary gates acting on an isolated system does not hold in practice. QUANTA therefore regards a quantum program as an open dynamical system, described by Kraus operators in discrete time and by the controlled Lindblad master equation in continuous time, and treats the choice of quantum gates as control decisions. The aim is to use control theory to design quantum algorithms, in particular optimisation algorithms, that are robust to noise and disturbances.

As a PhD student you will work mainly on two parts of the project. The first concerns reach-avoidance for quantum systems: computing the probability that a quantum process reaches a target set of states before it enters a set of forbidden states, and designing control strategies, for example by dynamic programming, that steer the computation towards its goal while respecting such constraints. You will develop this theory for quantum Markov chains described by Kraus operators and for continuous-time systems described by the Lindblad master equation.

The second part applies these results to quantum optimisation. You will develop algorithms in which an optimisation problem, starting with semidefinite programming and continuing with bilinear and polynomial problems, is solved by a quantum system regarded as a control system, including constrained problems formulated as reach-avoidance. You will analyse how the resulting quantum circuits scale with the problem size and test the algorithms on a real quantum computer.

You will work closely with the principal investigator, a postdoctoral researcher on the project and the project's international collaborators, and the project includes research stays at partner institutions abroad. You will present your results at international conferences and in scientific journals, and they will form the basis of your PhD thesis. As part of the PhD programme you will follow PhD courses and take part in teaching and supervision of student projects at the department.

Your competencies You hold a Master's degree in control engineering, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with a solid mathematical background, for example in linear algebra, dynamical systems, control theory, optimisation or probability theory, and with a genuine interest in quantum computing.

Knowledge of quantum mechanics or quantum information is an advantage, but not a requirement – what matters is that you are motivated to learn it during the project. Programming experience, for example in Python, is also an advantage. We value curiosity, the ability to work independently and the willingness to share ideas and help colleagues. You communicate well in English, both orally and in writing.

Qualification requirements

PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are

The position is hosted by the Learning and Decisions Lab at the Department of Electronic Systems, Aalborg University, led by Professor Rafal Wisniewski. The lab develops theory and algorithms at the intersection of control theory, stochastic systems, optimisation and quantum computing, including stability and safety of stochastic and quantum systems and feedback control of quantum hardware. You will join a team of senior researchers, PhD students and postdoctoral fellows working on related problems, in an informal and international environment with weekly meetings and close day-to-day supervision

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades)

• Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.

Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design

Salary and terms of employment

The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
